Prerequisite: A path from the FortiSandbox to the FortiGuard Distribution Network (FDN): DNS servers, a route, and firewalls that allow the connection, or a proxy or an overriding FDN server (FortiManager) set on the FortiGuard page
What it enables: FortiGuard module updates (antivirus signatures, engines, AI model), Web Filtering queries, and the Real-time Zero-Day Anti-Phishing service (P2 to P5); without it, package files must be downloaded from the Customer Service and Support site and uploaded by hand
How to put it in place: GUI: System > DNS (primary and secondary DNS servers); GUI: System > FortiGuard (FortiGuard Server Settings: overriding FDN server or Use Proxy; Update from FDN now); check the FDN and FortiGuard Services status in the Connectivity and services widget
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "FortiGuard" (FortiGuard Server Location, FortiGuard Server Settings, Upload Package File), "DNS Configuration", and "Connectivity and services widget" (FDN)

Prerequisite: A current FortiGuard Antivirus contract and the FortiSandbox engines (tracer and rating engine) licensed on the unit
What it enables: Antivirus signature and engine updates and the antivirus step of every scan
How to put it in place: Purchase the contract and check its expiry date and the engine status with vm-license -l and in the Connectivity and services widget (Antivirus and Engines, License required); GUI: System > FortiGuard (module versions and last update time)
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "Connectivity and services widget" (Antivirus: the date the antivirus database contract expires; Engines: License required) and "FortiGuard"; FortiSandbox 5.2.2 CLI Reference Guide, "vm-license" (Windows product keys and contract information, such as Antivirus and Web Filtering)

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard Web Filtering license on the unit
What it enables: Web Category ratings of URLs, the URL Pre-Filter, and the Web Category overrides, which come from queries to the FortiGuard Web Filtering Service
How to put it in place: Purchase the license and check it with vm-license -l and in the Connectivity and services widget (Web Filtering Query, License required)
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "Connectivity and services widget" (Web Filtering Query: License required) and "Web Category" (the FortiSandbox queries the FortiGuard Web Filtering Service)

Prerequisite: The Advanced Subscription (PAIX AI engine and model updates)
What it enables: Updates of the AI model after the initial model that comes with firmware 5.0.0 and later, and manual upload of the PAIX package
How to put it in place: Purchase the subscription and check the AI Engine and Model module in GUI: System > FortiGuard (module list); check the AI status in the Connectivity and services widget (License required)
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "Advanced AI" (subsequent AI model updates are part of the Advanced Subscription), "FortiGuard" (a valid PAIX subscription is required to upload the PAIX package manually), and "Connectivity and services widget" (AI: License required)

Prerequisite: A Real-time Zero-Day Anti-Phishing (RTAP) contract
What it enables: RTAP checks of URLs for phishing, spam, and malicious content, including URLs filtered out of the dynamic scan
How to put it in place: Purchase the contract, then select the Server Region in GUI: System > FortiGuard (FortiSandbox Real-time Zero-Day Anti-Phishing Service Settings); check the Anti-Phish status in the Connectivity and services widget
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "Real Time Anti-Phishing" (the RTAP service is subscription based), "FortiGuard" (Server Regions require a Real-time Zero-Day Anti-Phishing contract), and "Connectivity and services widget" (Anti-Phish: License required)

Prerequisite: Microsoft Windows and Office license keys for the guest VMs, one Windows key per clone of the matching edition, and enough VM clone capacity (base license of the model, UPG-LIC keys, or Universal VM subscription)
What it enables: Activation of the Windows guest VMs and Office in them, and so the dynamic (VM) scan of files and URLs; the number of clones that can be enabled
How to put it in place: Purchase the keys or licenses, download the license file from the Fortinet Customer Service and Support portal, and upload it in the System Information widget (Upload Windows/Office license on hardware, Upload VM License on VM models); check with vm-license -l and vm-status; GUI: Scan Policy and Object > VM Settings
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "VM Settings" (Model, License, and VM Information table; each clone requires its own retail license; Default Key, UPG-LIC, and Key_Only keys), "Upload license", and "Connectivity and services widget" (Win VM, MS Office, Universal VM: License required)

Prerequisite: Access from the FortiSandbox to the FortiGuard VM image server (fsavm.fortinet.net), directly or through a proxy
What it enables: Download of optional VMs, and of the default VMs on VM models where they are not pre-installed
How to put it in place: GUI: System > FortiGuard (VM Image Download Proxy Settings), then Tools > Add VMs from FortiGuard in GUI: Scan Policy and Object > VM Settings; check the VM Image status in the Connectivity and services widget
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "VM Settings" (To use the optional VM, Prerequisite: the VM image server fsavm.fortinet.net must be accessible) and "FortiGuard" (VM Image Download Proxy Settings)

Prerequisite: port3 connected to an isolated network behind a firewall that allows Internet access only (no route to protected subnets), with a next-hop gateway and DNS server
What it enables: Internet access of the guest VMs during dynamic scans (otherwise the simulated network, SIMNET, is used), and the Windows and Office activation of the guest VMs, which contacts Microsoft through port3
How to put it in place: vm-internet -s -g<GATEWAY> -d<DNS_SERVER>; or GUI: System > Settings (VM External Network Access); check the VM Internet status in the Connectivity and services widget
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "Interfaces" (port3 is isolated but can access the Internet; Office licenses are verified through the VMs, so Internet access through port3 is required) and "HA cluster pre-requisites" (port3 on all nodes connected to the Internet separately); FortiSandbox 5.2.2 CLI Reference Guide, "vm-internet"

Prerequisite: A Mail Transfer Agent (MTA) Service subscription, with enough per-mailbox seats for the monitored domains
What it enables: Scanning of email relayed through the MTA adapter (without a valid subscription, email is relayed without being scanned)
How to put it in place: Purchase the subscription (downloaded through FortiGuard, P1), then check the MTA contract in GUI: Security Fabric > Adapter (Click To View MTA Contract); vm-license -l
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "MTA adapter" (the adapter requires a subscription license with a per-mailbox seat count; email is relayed and not scanned if there is no valid MTA subscription license) and "Connectivity and services widget" (MTA: License required)

Prerequisite: The FortiGate, FortiMail, FortiWeb, FortiClient (EMS), FortiProxy, or FortiADC configured to send files to the FortiSandbox, and authorized on the FortiSandbox
What it enables: Device-mode submissions, verdicts and statistics returned to the device, and the malware and URL packages that the devices download
How to put it in place: Configure the FortiSandbox address on each device (see that device's documentation), then authorize it in GUI: Security Fabric > Device
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "Device" (only authorized devices, VDOMs, or protected domains can submit files; devices download the malware and URL packages)

Prerequisite: For inline block, a FortiGate running FortiOS 7.2 or later (or a FortiProxy) that reaches the FortiSandbox on port 4443 through an administrative or API port with HTTPS access enabled
What it enables: Inline block, where the device holds the file until the FortiSandbox verdict
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Interfaces (HTTPS access on the administrative or API port that receives the files), then the Inline Block Policy in GUI: Security Fabric > Device
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "Device" (Inline Block Policy: FortiGates running FOS v7.2 and higher; FortiSandbox must be reachable via port 4443; FortiGate connects only by an Admin or API port; FortiProxy Inline Block Policy) and "Interfaces" (ensure HTTPS is enabled for the port that receives inline block files)

Prerequisite: An ICAP client (a web proxy such as Squid or ProxySG) configured to send requests and responses to the FortiSandbox ICAP server
What it enables: ICAP adapter submissions, verdicts, and hold mode
How to put it in place: Configure the ICAP service on the proxy (the guide gives a squid.conf example), then the ICAP profile in GUI: Security Fabric > Adapter
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "ICAP adapter" (the proxy serves as the ICAP client; to configure an ICAP adapter, first configure the client)

Prerequisite: An upstream mail server that relays email to the FortiSandbox (MTA adapter) or forwards copies to it (BCC adapter), with the email domain resolving to the receiving FortiSandbox port
What it enables: MTA and BCC adapter submissions
How to put it in place: Configure the relay or BCC forwarding on the mail server, then the adapter in GUI: Security Fabric > Adapter
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "BCC Adapter" (receives forwarded emails from upstream MTA servers) and "MTA adapter" (email servers such as Sendmail relay emails to FortiSandbox over SMTP)

Prerequisite: A network share or cloud storage (SMB/CIFS share, AWS S3, Azure File System or Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage, Microsoft OneDrive or SharePoint, SFTP, NetApp StorageGRID) and an account with access to it
What it enables: Scheduled and event-driven network share scans, quarantine, and Netshare administrators
How to put it in place: Create the account on the storage, then the share in GUI: Security Fabric > Network Share (Create, then Test Connectivity)
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "Network Share" (network shares are scanned using the configured credentials; network share is available only on the primary node in an HA cluster) and "Cloud storage"

Prerequisite: Spanned switch ports or a network tap connected to FortiSandbox interfaces other than port1 and port3
What it enables: Sniffer mode: files, URLs, and network alerts extracted from the traffic, and TCP resets and replacement messages
How to put it in place: Configure the span port or tap on the network, then select the interfaces in GUI: Security Fabric > Sniffer
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "Sniffer" (sniffer mode relies on traffic from spanned switch ports; port1 and port3 cannot be used)

Prerequisite: An LDAP server, and for LDAPS or STARTTLS the CA certificate of the LDAP server (P20)
What it enables: Remote authentication of LDAP and LDAP wildcard administrators
How to put it in place: GUI: System > LDAP Servers; test with Test Login in GUI: System > Administrators
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "LDAP Servers", "Wildcard Admin Authentication", and "Certificates" (certificates are used for secure connections to an LDAP server)

Prerequisite: A primary RADIUS server (and a secondary), with any second factor enforced on the RADIUS server
What it enables: Remote authentication of RADIUS and RADIUS wildcard administrators, and RADIUS two-factor authentication
How to put it in place: GUI: System > RADIUS Servers; test with Test Login in GUI: System > Administrators
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "RADIUS Servers" and "Administrators" (when the RADIUS server is configured for two-factor authentication, users enter a token code)

Prerequisite: A SAML identity provider (Microsoft Entra ID or FortiAuthenticator) with the FortiSandbox registered as a service provider
What it enables: SAML single sign-on of administrators, and admin profiles assigned from the SAML assertion
How to put it in place: Register the SP metadata on the IdP, then import the IdP metadata in GUI: System > SAML SSO
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "SAML SSO" (with the Microsoft Entra ID and FortiAuthenticator examples)

Prerequisite: A FortiSandbox appliance, or an FSA-VM0T with the FortiToken Cloud service purchased
What it enables: Two-factor authentication (email, SMS, or FortiToken Mobile) for local administrators
How to put it in place: Purchase FortiToken Cloud for an FSA-VM0T, then set Two-factor Authentication on each local account in GUI: System > Administrators
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "Administrators" (Two-factor Authentication is only available for FortiSandbox appliances, and FSA-VM0T when FortiToken Cloud service is purchased); FortiSandbox 5.2.2 CLI Reference Guide, "system-admin"

Prerequisite: A server certificate and private key issued by the DoD PKI (or another approved CA) in .crt or .pem format, and the issuing CA certificates
What it enables: DoD-issued certificates for HTTPS and SSH administration, LDAPS, the ICAP server, and the MTA and BCC adapters (FortiSandbox does not generate certificates)
How to put it in place: Request the certificate from the CA, then import it and assign it to the service in GUI: System > Certificates (Import, Service)
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "Certificates" (certificates are used for secure connections to an LDAP server, HTTPS, SSH, the ICAP server, and the MTA adapter; FortiSandbox does not generate certificates) and "BCC Adapter" (server certificate)

Prerequisite: Remote log servers: syslog or CEF servers, a FortiAnalyzer, or FortiAnalyzer Cloud (with an access token, renewed every 90 days)
What it enables: Off-box logging of event, job, and alert logs, and secured logging to FortiAnalyzer
How to put it in place: GUI: Log & Report > Log Servers
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "Log Servers" (syslog over TCP or UDP, CEF, FortiAnalyzer, or FortiAnalyzer Cloud; the cloud token expires in 90 days; buffer of 1024 logs)

Prerequisite: An SMTP mail server and an account on it
What it enables: Malware detection notifications, scheduled reports, system resource status reports, and conserve mode alerts by email
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Mail Server (SMTP Server Address, Port 587 for STARTTLS, E-Mail Account, Login Account)
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "Mail Servers"

Prerequisite: An SNMP manager that receives the traps and polls the FortiSandbox, with the FortiSandbox MIB files loaded
What it enables: SNMP traps and SNMPv3 monitoring
How to put it in place: GUI: System > SNMP (SNMPv3 users with the manager address; download the MIB files)
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "SNMP" (Configuring the SNMP agent, MIB files, SNMP traps)

Prerequisite: An NTP server reachable from the FortiSandbox, preferably a DoD NTP server on the management network
What it enables: System time synchronization (FortiGuard or one NTP server)
How to put it in place: GUI: Dashboard > Status (System Information widget, System Time)
Source: Chapter row "System time and NTP synchronization (FortiGuard or one NTP server)" (the 4.0.0 Administration Guide); FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "HA cluster pre-requisites" (the system time must be synched on all nodes)

Prerequisite: An SCP or SFTP server (SCP or FTP for firmware and engine packages) reachable from the FortiSandbox, with an account and a directory
What it enables: Remote configuration backups and restores, and firmware and engine package uploads from a server
How to put it in place: GUI: System > System Recovery (Remote Backup: SCP or SFTP server, file path, user name, and schedule)
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "Remote Backup"; FortiSandbox 5.2.2 CLI Reference Guide, "backup-sysconf" and "fw-upgrade"

Prerequisite: The other HA cluster units: primary and secondary of the same model and configuration, all nodes on the same firmware build, port1 reachable between them, a dedicated port for internal cluster communication, and synchronized system time
What it enables: The HA cluster, its encrypted internal communication, and failover
How to put it in place: hc-settings -l; hc-status -l
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "HA cluster pre-requisites"; FortiSandbox 5.2.2 CLI Reference Guide, "hc-settings" and "hc-status"

Prerequisite: A FortiNDR server, installed and licensed, and an API key from it
What it enables: FortiNDR as an external verdict source
How to put it in place: Create the API key on FortiNDR, then enable it in GUI: Security Fabric > External Scan > FortiNDR
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "External Scan: FortiNDR" (Prerequisites: FortiNDR server is installed and licensed; the token from FortiNDR)

Prerequisite: An approved STIX/TAXII server, with a collection and an account on it
What it enables: Export of malware package intelligence in STIX format
How to put it in place: GUI: Threat Intelligence > Threat Intelligence Settings (STIX/TAXII Integration: API Root URL, TAXII Username, Collection ID)
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "Threat Intelligence Settings" (3. STIX/TAXII Integration)

Prerequisite: An approved WebHook server, such as FortiSOAR, with basic or token authentication
What it enables: Webhook callbacks of job verdicts
How to put it in place: GUI: Threat Intelligence > Threat Intelligence Settings (WebHook Integration, Test Connection)
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "Threat Intelligence Settings" (4. WebHook Integration)

Prerequisite: A model that supports encryption at rest: FortiSandbox VM, 500F, 1000F, 3000F, 500G, 1500G, or 3000G, not a cloud deployment (the TPM on the 500G, 1500G, and 3000G; HDD encryption with format-storage only on the 3000G)
What it enables: Data-at-rest encryption (DARE) and disk encryption
How to put it in place: Check the model in the System Information widget; set-dare-encryption -l
Source: FortiSandbox 5.2.2 Administration Guide, "Appendix H: Data At Rest Encryption (DARE)" (Enabling DARE mode); FortiSandbox 5.2.2 CLI Reference Guide, "format-storage" (the -k option is available only on FSA 3000G hardware appliances)
